svg.title: TwinPath Wrist June–September 2026 · ICRA 2027 submission, under review; second author Haitao Jiang, Yifan Liu, Yanbin Chang, Wei Zhang, Xiaogang Xiong, Hui Cheng† End-to-end real-to-real infrastructure: Independently built teleoperation, data collection, and π0.5/Diffusion Policy imitation-learning workflows from scratch for UR5e, a custom wrist, and different end effectors, using equipment shared by RAPID (Prof. Hui Cheng) and MMLab (Prof. Ping Luo). Supported four configurations—Wuji hand, custom wrist + Wuji hand, gripper, and custom wrist + gripper—for fixed-versus-enabled wrist experiments. Teleoperation: Used a SpaceMouse to control the 6-DoF UR5e, wuji-retargeting (the official adaptation of dex-retargeting) for the 20-DoF Wuji hand, and a custom master wrist built by a senior lab member for the 2-DoF follower wrist. Data collection: Frequent jumps in thumb–index distance during grasping prompted replacing real-time wuji-retargeting with keyboard-selected gesture presets, reducing control complexity and improving data stability. Integrated motion planning and saved key poses for rapid homing and preset-pose switching, reserving manual teleoperation for difficult subtasks. Built web-based visualization and hand-temperature alerts. Compared with the conventional SpaceMouse/dex-retargeting workflow, this process enabled inexperienced operators to collect 40+ successful demonstrations in 30 minutes. Imitation learning: Investigated grasp misalignment and weak generalization during Wuji-hand picking. Disabled camera inputs one at a time and found that removing one view barely changed policy trajectories. Added training perturbations and random camera/state input dropout; the retrained policy completed the pick test task.
